sections.notes: Repeated component definition and anatomy illustration only.

sections.title: Placement
sections.notes: Stacked settings layouts are described as common placement, not as a required arrangement.

checks.statement: M3 switches use updated color mappings that meet non-text contrast requirements and support dynamic color, have a taller and wider track, and may include an icon in the handle; the updated presentation improves accessibility.
checks.condition: When implementing M3 switches or migrating from M2.

sourceHistory.summary: M2 comparison lists switch track, color, accessibility, and optional handle-icon changes.

evidence.result: Track width/height, outline and color are sourced from the switch token bindings; the state size and icon slots are separately tokenized.

checks.statement: Use on-surface for the adjacent text label in all interaction states; supporting text may use on-surface-variant.
checks.condition: When styling text next to a switch.

sourceHistory.summary: Adjacent-label section specifies label and optional supporting-text color roles.

evidence.result: The switch input carries a configured aria-label, but no visible adjacent text is rendered by this specimen and the adjacent-label color state cannot be confirmed.

implementation.notes: Visible label color behavior is not represented in this example.

checks.statement: Represent enabled, hovered, focused, pressed, and disabled states.

sourceHistory.summary: State diagram caption lists five switch states.

evidence.result: Checked, disabled and focus-visible states are explicit; the local rules do not establish hover and pressed appearance across all on/off combinations.

implementation.notes: Full hover/pressed state rendering was not observed.

checks.statement: Use a 52×32dp track with 2dp outline and full corners; 16dp unselected handle, 24dp selected or icon-bearing handle, and 28dp pressed handle; 40dp state layer and 48dp target. Selected and unselected icons are 16dp.
checks.condition: When sizing switches and their interaction target.

sourceHistory.summary: Measurements table specifies track, handle, state-layer, target, and icon dimensions by state.

evidence.result: The invisible native checkbox covers the control target; track, handle and state-layer dimensions use their specific token variables.

checks.statement: Use switches for standalone settings or options that immediately toggle one binary value on/off or true/false. The effect should take place immediately without saving. Use them for independently controlled list items, not mutually exclusive opposing options or actions requiring a separate save.
checks.condition: When choosing a switch for a setting or list.

sourceHistory.summary: Usage guidance defines binary immediate settings and distinguishes switch from opposing choices and save-based selection.

implementation.notes: Choosing a standalone binary setting and whether changes save immediately is product behavior, not decided by the switch primitive.

checks.statement: Use checkboxes for multiple related list selections, radio buttons for one selection from a list, and switches for standalone or verbose settings. Use a connected button group for opposing options and a button for a call to action.
checks.condition: When choosing among switch, checkbox, radio button, and button-group controls.

sourceHistory.summary: Alternate-control guidance maps selection cardinality and action type to components.

implementation.notes: Choosing switch versus checkbox, radio, connected group or action button depends on the product interaction model.

checks.statement: A handle icon is optional and should clearly and unambiguously communicate the on/off selection. Avoid ambiguous or non-binary icons.
checks.condition: When adding an icon to a switch handle.

sourceHistory.summary: Icon guidance specifies selection meaning and warns against ambiguous imagery.

implementation.notes: The meaning of optional on/off handle glyphs is a content choice; the specimen does not include descriptive visible labels.

checks.statement: Always pair a switch with inline text describing what it controls when on; keep the label short and direct. Do not put text inside the switch because it becomes too small to be accessible; use a suitable icon instead.

sourceHistory.summary: Label guidance requires an external inline label and prohibits small text inside the control.

evidence.result: The visible option label names its native input via aria-labelledby and activates it via for/id.
Both specimen renderings contain unique matching input, label and accessible-name references.
Chromium: six assertions pass for visible names, associations and toggling by clicking the label.

fixes.summary: Label checkbox and switch examples with visible text

checks.statement: On interaction, slide the handle to the other end of the track and apply the corresponding action immediately; change handle size to indicate the on state and interaction.

sourceHistory.summary: Behavior guidance describes sliding, immediate action, and handle-size feedback.

evidence.result: The native checkbox owns toggling and checked state moves the handle to the opposite end with a token-driven transition.

checks.statement: Assistive-technology users must be able to navigate to and toggle the switch with keyboard or switch input and receive feedback appropriate to the input type.

sourceHistory.summary: Use cases list navigation, toggling, and input-appropriate feedback.

evidence.result: A native checkbox is exposed with role=switch, an accessible name, and disabled/checked state.

checks.statement: On touch tap/drag and cursor click, grow the handle; on hover in either state, grow the hover area and change the cursor to show interactivity.
checks.condition: When a switch is interacted with by touch or cursor.

sourceHistory.summary: Interaction guidance specifies handle and hover-area growth and cursor feedback.

evidence.result: The feedback circle grows from 80% to full size on hover, focus and press using motion tokens. Existing handle growth remains. The hit area does not change.
Chromium: ten assertions pass across both states for feedback scaling, handle feedback, target stability and reduced motion.

fixes.summary: Grow switch feedback without moving its hit target

checks.statement: Do not apply density by default because it can reduce targets below 48×48 CSS pixels. If offering density control, keep its own targets at least 48×48 CSS pixels so people can change it back.
checks.condition: When offering compact switch layouts or density settings.

sourceHistory.summary: Density guidance sets default behavior and minimum target size for reversal controls.

implementation.notes: No switch density control is offered in this implementation, so the conditional minimum target for a reversible density setting does not apply.

checks.statement: Place initial focus directly on the switch handle.
checks.condition: When a switch receives initial focus.

sourceHistory.summary: Initial-focus section identifies the handle as the primary interactive element.

evidence.result: The transparent native checkbox is the actual focusable control and overlays the full switch target; focus-visible styling is drawn around the switch.

checks.statement: Tab focuses the switch handle; Space or Enter toggles it on or off.

sourceHistory.summary: Keyboard table maps Tab and activation keys.

evidence.result: Enter invokes native input.click once; repeats do not toggle. Space and Tab remain native.
Switch activation regression passes for Enter, repeat, disabled and native Space preservation.
Chromium: six assertions pass for toggle/change counts, retained focus, repeats and disabled behavior; pre-fix page failed Enter.

fixes.summary: Support native switch activation with Enter

checks.statement: Use adjacent label text as the switch accessibility label when it clearly describes the function; make it more descriptive when the visible wording is ambiguous. The screen reader announces the UI text followed by the switch role.
checks.condition: When exposing a switch to assistive technology.

sourceHistory.summary: Labeling guidance specifies adjacent text and expanded accessibility wording when needed.

evidence.result: The input role=switch receives c.Label() as its accessible name, followed by the platform-provided switch role.

checks.statement: Support switches without icons, with an icon in the selected state only, and with icons in both selected and unselected states.

sourceHistory.summary: Configuration section lists no icons, selected-only icon, and icons in both states.

evidence.result: CSS can suppress icons when data-with-icon is false and distinguishes on/off icon visibility, but the specimen always renders both SVGs and does not show selected-only versus both-icon configuration wiring.

implementation.notes: The configuration attribute binding is not visible in this specimen.
